title: Inverse image along an open immersion is a left inverse of direct image
statement:
Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. The counit $j^{-1}j_*\to\mathrm{id}$ on $\Ab(U_{\Et})$ is a natural isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every $F\in D(U_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the canonical Leray morphism
$$\RGamma(X_{\Et},Rj_*F)\longrightarrow\RGamma(U_{\Et},F)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf Z)$. Here $Rj_*$ is the total right derived direct image computed by K-injective resolutions [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], and $\RGamma$ is the unbounded derived global sections of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. On bounded-below complexes this is the inverse of the isomorphism of [lem-kun-leray-bdd].

proof.text: The existing open-immersion fully-faithfulness statement [lem-sc-open-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful] says that the direct image $j_*:\Ab(U_{\Et})\to\Ab(X_{\Et})$ is fully faithful, equivalently that the counit $j^{-1}j_*G\to G$ is an isomorphism for every abelian sheaf $G$ on $U_{\Et}$. Thus the counit gives the asserted natural isomorphism $j^{-1}j_*\cong\mathrm{id}$.

Choose a complex $C$ representing $F$ and a K-injective resolution $C\to I$ by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], taking the coefficient ring to be $\mathbf Z$. The functor $j^{-1}$ is additive and exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], and is left adjoint to $j_*$ by [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; $j_*$ is additive by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $u=j_*$, $v=j^{-1}$. It follows that $j_*I$ is K-injective on $X_{\Et}$. No bound on $I$, no quasi-compactness, and no finite cohomological dimension is used.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, label lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; unbounded replacement exists as in the cited resolution node

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to termwise $j_*$ followed by localization. An additive termwise functor commutes with shifts and with the cone matrix (its entries are differentials, maps, and their negatives); hence it gives an exact functor on homotopy categories, as required there. The same observation applies to termwise global sections. Thus $Rj_*F$ is represented by $j_*I$, and, since both $I$ and $j_*I$ are K-injective, [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] computes the two derived-global-sections objects by $\Gamma(X,j_*I)$ and $\Gamma(U,I)$. By [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], in degree $r$ the former is $I^r(X\times_XU)$. The projection $p:X\times_XU\to U$ has inverse $(j,\mathrm{id}_U)$; both inverse identities follow from the uniqueness clause of [def-pc-fibre-product]. Restriction along $p^{-1}$ therefore gives $I^r(X\times_XU)\cong I^r(U)$. Naturality of restriction with respect to the sheaf morphism $d_I^r$ makes these isomorphisms commute with differentials, so they give an isomorphism of complexes $\Gamma(X,j_*I)\cong\Gamma(U,I)$. Its derived class is an isomorphism with the displayed source and target.

proof.text: For a morphism $F\to F'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy class of maps $h:I\to I'$ between the chosen K-injective representatives. In each degree, the two composites from $I^r(X\times_XU)$ to $I'^r(U)$ agree because $h^r$ commutes with sheaf restriction. Thus the chain isomorphism of Step 3 is natural. Applying additive $j_*$ and $\Gamma$ termwise preserves homotopies. A change of K-injective representative is a homotopy equivalence by the same Hom bijection (lift the derived inverse and use injectivity to check the inverse identities), and the preceding restriction square identifies the two comparisons. Hence this is the canonical derived comparison induced by the underived sections identification, independent of resolutions. For $F$ bounded below, choose a bounded-below injective representative as in [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Its direct image is bounded below and K-injective by Step 2; [lem-kun-rgamma-unbounded-bounded] identifies the bounded and unbounded global-section computations. The comparison of [lem-kun-leray-bdd] is induced by the same underived sections identification in the opposite direction. Therefore our map is its inverse on that subcategory, while the construction above supplies it for all $F\in D(U_{\Et})$.
